bug_semantics: Scriban's template builtin array.insert_at (ArrayFunctions.InsertAt) pads the target list by running a tight C# for-loop from list.Count up to an attacker-controlled index and calling Add(null) each step, then Inserts the value. That fill never calls TemplateContext.StepLoop and never consults LoopLimit, LimitToString, RecursiveLimit, or ObjectRecursionLimit, even though LoopLimit (default 1000) existed from the first commit for script for-statements. A one-line template such as {{ [1] | array.insert_at 200000000 'x' | array.size }} therefore allocates unbounded memory, raises OutOfMemoryException, and can terminate the host process in well under a second. The 7.0.0 sibling hardening (dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9) added StepLoop overloads to other ArrayFunctions primitives and still left InsertAt on the unbounded IEnumerable/int/object signature. CVE-2026-74784 / first-party GHSA-24c8-4792-22hx: affected <= 7.1.0 (CVE < 7.2.0); patched 7.2.0.

The commit object has no parent line, git rev-parse 46054810^ fails, and git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD is this SHA, so no finer public member exists.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-74784 is a published VulnCheck CVE wrapping the live first-party advisory GHSA-24c8-4792-22hx (reviewed, not withdrawn). The sink is the array.insert_at fill that allocates index-Count nulls in compiled C# without StepLoop. That loop is present on 7.1.0 and absent as a reachable template primitive after 7fdf19df / 7.2.0, matching the patched boundary. BIC search used git log -S/-L and parent absence, not an AI-marked commit hunt: the smallest public first-write of the fill is root commit 46054810 (2016-01-25). Later ArrayFunctions edits only relocated or retyped the same loop (copy-on-write, argument order, ScriptRange). Incomplete 7.0.0 LoopLimit hardening is a missed sibling, not the introducer. AI judgment is BIC-commit-object only: Alexandre Mutel author and committer, empty trailers, no bot, 2016 initial import. Therefore a real vulnerability with human authorship: NOT_AI. The 7.2.0 merge-from-fork is the direct fix; private-fork members are not reconstructable in public history, which does not affect BIC choice.
